cards.text: This one's a song of ascents, and Israel gets told to say it out loud. Israel's line goes, "Many a time they have persecuted me from my youth". From YOUTH, friend, that's not a rough week, that's a rough LIFE.
Then Israel says that line again, word for word. But this time, friend, the line keeps going.

cards.question: Israel has been persecuted again and again since youth. How does it turn out for the ones doing the persecuting?

answers.text: They have not won against Israel
They finally broke Israel's spirit
They wore Israel down to nothing

cards.question: Israel describes what all that persecution felt like. What picture does Israel use for its own back?

answers.text: A field the plowmen plowed over
A wall the builders tore down
A road the soldiers marched on

cards.text: And they made their furrows long, friend. Meanwhile I did a few years in the back of a junk drawer and called THAT rough.
But right here, the song turns. Israel stops talking about the plowmen and starts talking about the LORD.

cards.question: After all those years of persecution, Israel calls the LORD righteous.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Israel has been plowed over again and again. What does Israel say the LORD has done?

answers.text: Cut Israel from the cords of the wicked
Paid the plowmen back twice over
Given Israel a quiet field of its own

cards.text: Israel was tied up like a cookie box with the string knotted three times. And the LORD just goes SNIP, done, NEXT!

cards.question: Then the psalm turns to all who hate Zion. It says may they be turned back in ___.

answers.text: shame
peace
glory

cards.text: And the psalm has a picture for them too. May they be like grass on the rooftops.

cards.question: Grass on the rooftops ___ before it can grow.

answers.text: withers
drowns
freezes

cards.question: When the reaper comes by, the rooftop grass gives him a full armload to carry.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Not enough to fill the reaper's hands or the arms of the binder of sheaves. That's me opening the oven for a full tray and finding ONE crumb, just standing there in my apron like, "Where'd my batch go?"

cards.question: Last line. People walk past the ones who hate Zion. What does the psalm wish none of them would say?

answers.text: The blessing of the LORD be on you
Your fields will be full next year
Come and rest with us tonight

cards.text: Not even a "we bless you in the name of the LORD" from anybody walking by. The psalm wishes them no blessing at all.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. Verse 4 (the LORD cut Israel from the cords of the wicked) was already given on card 8, so the card only replays it as a joke and does not move the baker forward.

The right answer is the only one with Bible phrasing and the only one that names the LORD. The wrong answers ('Your fields will be full next year', 'Come and rest with us tonight') are plain everyday wishes, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'The psalm wishes them no blessing at all' stretches verse 8. The verse only wishes that none who pass by would speak the blessing over them. It does not wish them no blessing of any kind.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The joke gives the LORD a comic catchphrase ('the LORD just goes SNIP, done, NEXT!'). It isn't mocking God, but it makes the LORD the comic voice of the punchline.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin's jokes put playful made-up words or sound effects in the LORD's mouth, or does the reverence rule ('His humor never targets God') also rule out making God the speaker of a punchline?

findings.problem: The two wrong answers ('They finally broke Israel's spirit' and 'They wore Israel down to nothing') mean nearly the same thing as each other. A baker can rule them both out as a pair and pick the right answer without understanding verse 2.
findings.question: Should the answer rules also forbid two wrong answers that mean the same thing as each other? The current 'No near-matches' rule only covers a wrong answer that is close to the right answer.
